body:
#2064 (BUG-1464) APPROVED at f64b93caf9bc. One finding, and the referent rule
got its first real outing on a PR rather than in a discussion.

THE CORE CLAIM IS ASSERTED IN ITS STRONGEST AVAILABLE FORM, which is worth
naming because the weaker forms were all available: "preserve existing role
TOML byte-for-byte" is checked with `refreshed.starts_with(legacy)`. Not field
equality, not a parse round-trip — a prefix assertion on the raw bytes, which
proves the existing content is untouched AND that the prompt was APPENDED
rather than the file rewritten. A field-level check would have passed a
re-serialisation that reordered keys or normalised whitespace, and that is
exactly the failure a TOML rewrite produces.

THE CLAUDE.md UPDATE EXPLAINS THE ASYMMETRY RATHER THAN RECORDING IT: "Starter
roles predate those markers, so refresh only appends a shipped system_prompt
when that field is absent." That answers the question a reader would otherwise
ask — why roles are handled unlike every other pack — and it is the kind of
reason that stops someone "fixing" the inconsistency in six months.

I APPLIED THE REFERENT RULE TO THE PROSE THIS PR EDITS. The paragraph cites
aida-core/src/scaffolding/refresh.rs and aida-cli-lib/src/scaffold_refresh.rs;
both exist at this head. Checked, not assumed — the rule is cheap enough that
running it is less effort than deciding whether to.

THE FINDING: THE THIRD CLAIMED COVERAGE IS COMMENT-PROTECTED, NOT
TEST-PROTECTED. The body lists "legacy refresh, custom prompt survival, and
silent no-op behavior". The test covers the first two. For the third I found
only TWO COMMENTS — a doc comment at :307 and an inline note at :465 — and
ZERO is-none assertions in the added lines.

AND THIS PR IS PRECISELY WHAT MAKES IT MATTER: it PROMOTES that behaviour into
CLAUDE.md as a documented contract ("packs you never installed are not
created"). The mechanism is starter_roles_refresh() returning None. If a later
change returned Some(empty report), a user who never installed roles would see
a roles pack, the documented contract would be false, and nothing would fail.

A CONTRACT WHOSE ONLY GUARD IS A COMMENT is the shape we have catalogued all
day — and here the PR has just upgraded a comment-guarded behaviour into a
published promise without upgrading its guard. One test asserting None when no
roles dir exists closes it. Not blocking: the behaviour is correct today and
the comments are accurate.

Noted separately on the verdict: the body's "Closes BUG-1464" is a GitHub
issue-closing keyword, not an AIDA trailer. It has no effect on spec status
and should not be read as one — the actual trailer is in the subject, and both
artefacts agree here.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2064 approved - it promotes a comment-guarded behaviour into a CLAUDE.md contract without upgrading its guard. Referent rule ran on its prose and passed
